notes: The operator GT plan identifies the complete northern triangle, direct eastern junction and outer hairpin, and central S-shaped connector. This repairs the previous shortcut through the northern triangle and incorrect eastern short course. Exact pinned public OSM nodes retain the western course, current mapped western bend, northern triangle and eastern return. The missing central connector is independently located on the licensed 2020 one-metre Environment Agency intensity survey. Public node segments, parent snapshot hash, connector pixel vertices, native survey mosaic, tile hashes and reprojection are preserved in the accompanying import metadata. OSM node coordinates are converted into the survey pixel grid without fitting them to private coordinates or lengths. The geometry combines ODbL public nodes with an OGL survey connector; both attributions are retained. Private course diagrams identify branches only. Native survey lane selection, later pavement changes and operator versus catalogue distance differences remain draft. Independent public-node and surveyed-connector course: 5907.1 m. Direction, historical configuration and fine corner alignment remain draft; no course coordinates come from the comparison catalogue.

sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 80 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the mapped trace, not an official length measurement. The saved start gate sets the simulation origin. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.
